Purchased in Target on a whim and works in my basic K15 model Keurig.  I use a Keurig machine every day.  I would only use the filter if I had no K Cups in the house and needed coffee in the morning while really rushed for time.  Since I have other ways of making coffee using bagged coffee, I would use one of those methods if I had time.  The filter works as intended but the coffee produced with 2 tablespoons of ground coffee is even weaker than K Cup coffee.  I guess the problem is the Keurig model I have does not allow for controlling the amount of time it takes for the water to go through the filter.  As it is, the water rushes through this filter seemingly faster than with a K Cup, although I have not timed it.  I will keep it in reserve in case I am desperate.  Construction quality seems fine with thick plastic.  I do not see how this is really cost effective though.  With a drip coffee maker I usually only use one tablespoon to each cup and get coffee that is strong and flavorful enough for me.
